column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves both Uzziah and the dead king unnamed, using he and the king; BSB supplies both names.
The Hebrew gives the mother’s name and origin without a separate she was clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes Zechariah as understanding the seeing of God; BSB describes instruction in the fear of God.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed and repeats wall for each city; BSB names Uzziah and combines the walls.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says his name went to the entrance of Egypt; BSB speaks of fame and the border.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew twice describes the registration and direction through a hand; BSB uses recorded and under the direction.
The Hebrew calls the families fathers.
The Hebrew pictures authority as their hand and speaks of a singular enemy; BSB uses authority and plural enemies.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew pairs inventions with an inventor and says he was helped until he became strong; BSB uses skillfully designed and so that.
The Hebrew pictures arrogance as the heart rising high.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls Aaron’s descendants sons.

The Hebrew explicitly names a separate house and says Jotham judged the people; BSB uses isolation and governing.
The Hebrew has Isaiah actively writing the account; BSB uses a passive recording.
The Hebrew has unnamed plural agents burying him; BSB makes burial passive.
